subject: Request: One-time 'golden hour' pricing exemption for Artemis Health POC
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T08:12:00Z
Subject: Request: one-time pricing exemption for Artemis POC

Kimberly / Marissa,

Quick heads-up — Artemis (Aisha + Devon) just pushed a hard deadline: they want a signed SOW and invoice in the next 6 hours to start a 30-day POC next week. They’re asking for a one-time 40% discount off list for the POC period (volume: ~1.2M tokens/day projected). Customer cites competing vendor offering very aggressive pilot economics; losing momentum risks the whole deal.

Attached: Artemis_SOW_v2.pdf and pricing-breakdown.xlsx.

Why I’m asking for an exception:
- Time pressure: procurement will sign only if terms are in the invoice immediately.
- Upside: if POC shows model fit, they’ve indicated potential to convert to a committed annual contract (~$750k ARR) in Q1.
- Risk: 40% would be outside the revenue ops guardrails without VP/CFO signoff (and above our standard pilot concession).

Requested ask: Can we authorize a one-time, limited "golden hour" exemption to grant up to 40% off for the POC, with the following conditions:
- Discount valid only for this single invoice/SOW (no roll-forward)
- Customer signs an explicit conversion commitment term (30-day POC -> 6-month/commit if conversion within 60 days) or we require a bump-back clause
- Legal to add standard make-good clause and data residency addendum

If approval is possible, I’ll send the customer the redlined SOW and invoice immediately. If not, I need a clear fallback (max % we can offer) so I can respond within their window.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: one-time pricing exemption for Artemis POC

Rishi —

Appreciate the context and the attached materials. A few quick notes:

1) Our standard pilot concession matrix caps pre-approved discounts at 25% for deals under $1M ARR expectation without VP/CFO approval. This request is clearly outside that.
2) We should ask Finance (Marcus) for a conditional cap and Revenue Ops (Marissa) to validate the proposed conversion language in the SOW before we push to Legal.

Initial recommendation (to avoid losing momentum): propose a compromise — offer 30% for the POC limited to 30 days, with the customer signing an LOI to convert to a 6-month minimum within 60 days at an agreed blended rate. If they insist on 40% we take escalated approval from Marcus with a short memo.

Marcus — looping you for finance perspective and whether a 35% one-time concession is something you would consider for this class of account if legal + revops put the conversion guardrails in place.

Marissa — if you can draft the one-page approval memo (redwood-approval-form.docx) with recommended controls, we’ll route to Marcus and copy VP/CFO if Marcus signs off. Timing is tight so a quick bullet-style memo is perfect.

Best,
Kimberly

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: one-time pricing exemption for Artemis POC

Thanks — put together a short approval packet (attached: redwood-approval-form.docx). Summary below for Marcus and finance:

- Customer: Artemis Health (contact: Aisha Patel / Devon Lee)
- Proposed concession: one-time 40% off list for 30-day POC
- ARR upside: potential $750k ARR if conversion to a committed plan within 90 days
- Controls we require before approval:
  - Signed SOW that includes conversion commitment language (minimum 6-month term or explicit renewal discount removal)
  - Legal-approved make-good and audit clause
  - Finance to mark deal as "pilot concession" in SFDC with a conversion checkpoint and clawback policy if they don't convert

My suggestion for Marcus: authorize up to 35% as a Finance-acceptable ceiling for immediate go/no-go. If Marcus approves 35% we can offer 35 instantly and tell the customer we need to iterate on the SOW for conversion terms. If Marcus wants to escalate, we can route to VP/CFO.

Rishi — I also added two optional downstream mitigations inside the packet: a short-term seat cap on ingestion, plus a one-time usage threshold that if exceeded will trigger a billing review. Both protect us against an oversized pilot burn.

Let me know and I’ll finalize the memo for Marcus to sign.

—Marissa

Attachment: redwood-approval-form.docx

Date: 2027-10-02T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: one-time pricing exemption for Artemis POC — conditional approval

Team — after reviewing the packet and projected conversion economics, I will authorize a conditional, one-time concession for this scenario with the following firm constraints:

1) Approved concession: up to 35% off list for this single 30-day POC invoice (not to be repeated).
2) Customer must sign the updated SOW that includes both: a conversion commitment (6-month minimum if they convert within 60 days) and a clawback clause that triggers a retroactive bill if conversion triggers do not occur.
3) Billing must flag the invoice as "pilot concession — conditional approval 2027-10-02" and route through Finance for tracking.
4) Legal needs to append the standard make-good and audit language before sending.

Once Marissa uploads the finalized redwood-approval-form.docx with the controls and Rishi confirms the redlined SOW, proceed to send to the customer and close the loop here. If Artemis insists on 40%, we will not approve without explicit VP/CFO escalation.

Marcus Lin
SVP, Finance | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
